clue.text: A stiff examination

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, so this is the medical inspection of a dead body, not a demanding test

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' reads as an adjective meaning hard or severe; it is really the noun, slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is the examination of a corpse to establish the cause of death.

clue.text: Direction signs causing a dispute within royal society

indicators.note: the dispute sits inside the letters for royal society, so within signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's scientific academy
a row is a noisy quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Some signage provokes a quarrel among the fellows of a learned royal society.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointers on signposts showing which way to go are drawn as these shapes with heads.

clue.text: Servant blowing top working in inn

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
to lose or blow one's top is to have the head removed, so the first letter of the word servant goes

explanation.surface: A servant loses their temper while working in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' drops the S of SERVANT, leaving ERVANT, and 'working' rearranges those letters. 'Blowing top' looks like losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an old word for a pub or alehouse where drink and lodging are sold.

clue.text: Comic put right about soprano born in us port

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the two single letters, so about signals one piece wrapping another
comic means funny or ridiculous, so the letters of the phrase put right are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for soprano in music
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A comedian corrects something about a soprano born in an American harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' rearranges PUT RIGHT into PITTURGH, and 'about' wraps that round S and B.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pennsylvania city stands where three rivers meet and has long been a major inland river harbour.

clue.text: Coarse type in hostelry, a hooker

indicators.note: in says the answer is found sitting inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rough character is found in a pub alongside a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across hostelrY A HOOker. A yahoo is the brutish creature from Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish, uncouth person is called by the name of Swift's brutish humanlike creatures.

clue.text: Unpaid, a foreign RU team

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters of RU team are turned into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: RU is rugby union; these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas rugby union side plays without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' works only on the letters after the A; RU is the usual crossword shorthand for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays a sport without receiving payment is a non-professional.

clue.text: In one action — easy to a skater

indicators.note: easy, as in the order to relax or ease off, signals that the letters of to a skater are loosened into another order

explanation.surface: Something done in a single move comes easily to someone on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easy' rearranges the letters of TO A SKATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with a single blow or movement means doing it all at once.

clue.text: Support a Verdi opera

parts.note: to aid is to help or support

explanation.surface: A request to back one of Verdi's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi wrote this opera set in ancient Egypt, first staged in Cairo in 1871.

clue.text: Visual faculty certainly needed in rowing crew

indicators.note: the word for certainly has to go into the word for the boat crew, so needed in signals insertion

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat with eight rowers, or its crew
yes, as an emphatic agreement, means certainly

explanation.surface: Good vision is undoubtedly essential for those in a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing crew' suggests oarsmen in general; in rowing an eight is the specific boat and its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The power of seeing is the sense by which we perceive things visually.

clue.text: Mountain in the black hills with four faces

definitions.text: Mountain in the black hills with four faces

parts.words: Mountain in the black hills with four faces
parts.note: a South Dakota peak in the Black Hills range into which the heads of four US presidents are carved

explanation.walkthrough: The four faces are the giant carvings of Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt and Lincoln, not the sides of a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Dakota monument carved with four presidents' heads stands on this granite peak.

clue.text: Bolt in iron tripod with no head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the word for the iron stand loses its opening letter

parts.note: a trivet is a small three-legged iron stand for a pot or kettle by the fire

explanation.surface: A bolt is fixed in a headless iron tripod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' removes the first letter T from TRIVET.
explanation.definitionFit: A short metal pin hammered flat to fasten plates together is a kind of bolt.

clue.text: The crown making explosive speech?

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
an address is a formal speech to an audience

explanation.surface: The monarch delivers a fiery, explosive oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The crown' reads as the monarchy, but it is something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is a piece of regalia worn on the head, so it is one kind of headgear.

clue.text: Poet attaching merit to argument

parts.note: to have words with someone is to argue, so words means an argument
worth is value or merit

explanation.surface: A poet joins merit to a reasoned case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attaching ... to' puts the merit after the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet who wrote Daffodils.

clue.text: Strong business partnership

definitions.meaning: a company or partnership of professionals

explanation.surface: A robust commercial alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means solid or unyielding; a firm is also a company, especially one run by partners.

clue.text: I witnessed struggling test side

indicators.note: struggling means floundering, so the letters of I witnessed are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone saw a Test cricket team in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges the letters of I WITNESSED. A Test is a full international cricket match, and the Caribbean nations play as one team.
explanation.definitionFit: The combined Caribbean cricket team plays international Test matches under this name.

clue.text: Cooperate, using influence to pay back that woman

parts.note: pull is influence, as in having pull with the boss
to get someone is to pay them back or take revenge, as in I'll get you
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone works with others, using their clout to settle a score with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To work together as a team for a common goal is to collaborate.

clue.text: Girl entertaining friend, old lady, here in the canary islands

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them inside one's home, so the girl's word holds the other letters

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland
a pal is a friend
ma, like old lady, is informal for mother

explanation.surface: A girl has a friend and her mother to stay on holiday in the Canaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is British slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Gran Canaria is a large city in the Spanish island group off Africa.

clue.text: Well-read, two accounts about ms Moore?

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, used here twice

indicators.note: the second account goes round the actress's first name, so about signals one piece wrapping another

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account again
Demi Moore is the American film actress

explanation.surface: Is the actress Demi Moore well read, judging by a couple of reports?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Ms Moore stands for her first name only, the actress Demi.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and learned, someone bookish and studious is described this way.

clue.text: Lamb frolicking by said castle

indicators.note: frolicking means playing about, so the letters of lamb skip into a new order

parts.note: oral means spoken or said aloud

explanation.surface: A lamb gambols beside a castle that someone mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges LAMB into BALM. Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal family's Scottish home is a castle on Deeside in Aberdeenshire.

clue.text: Police documents showing exact ropes

parts.note: to exact a payment is to demand or charge it
on a sailing boat, sheets are the ropes that control the sails

explanation.surface: Police papers reveal the precise ropes used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' reads as the adjective meaning precise, but it is the verb, to demand payment.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the records kept at a British police station listing the offences a suspect is accused of.

clue.text: Fix up extremely remarkable couple

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of the word remarkable are kept

parts.note: a pair is a couple, two of a kind

explanation.surface: Patch up a truly extraordinary twosome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of remarkable, R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something broken is to restore it to working order.

clue.text: Stick plug in this place

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement, shortened to ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Push a plug into this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests a stopper; it is a promotion or advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or bond firmly to something is to be glued fast to it.

clue.text: Obscure English coin found in the us

parts.note: dim means faint or obscure

explanation.surface: A rare English coin has turned up in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective describing the coin, but it gives a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: The American ten-cent piece is a small silver-coloured coin.

clue.text: First leader from a Berkshire town

parts.note: maiden means first, as in a maiden voyage or maiden speech
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: The first leader came from a town in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London; the town lies on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thames-side town lies in the English county of Berkshire, west of London.

clue.text: Nightclub took off? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word for took off is used, the first five of its ten letters

parts.note: discounted means took off a sum from the price

explanation.surface: Did the nightclub become popular? It certainly did!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for an emphatic yes, but here it keeps only the first half of DISCOUNTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A club where people dance to recorded pop music is a night spot of this kind.

clue.text: Member's from a town in Cheshire, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the town's name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Lymm is a small town in Cheshire, in north-west England, pronounced like lim

explanation.surface: Someone is said to come from a Cheshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lymm is a Cheshire village-town in north-west England whose name rhymes with him.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a bodily member.

clue.text: Bird produced by mother on Sunday feast day

parts.note: a martin is a small bird of the swallow family
ma is informal for mother

explanation.surface: A bird cooked by mother on Sunday for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Martinmas, 11 November, is the feast of St Martin, once a traditional time to slaughter and eat livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian festival of St Martin falls on 11 November.

clue.text: Incensed upright character, judge

parts.note: the capital letter I is a single upright stroke
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: An honest person is outraged and wants to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' reads as an honest person; it is a letter of the alphabet standing straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious or angry is in a rage.

clue.text: Famous people touring eastern sulawesi

indicators.note: the famous people travel round the letter for eastern, so touring signals one piece going round another

parts.note: celebs is short for celebrities, famous people

explanation.surface: Celebrities on a tour of the east of an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts E inside CELEBS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island now called Sulawesi was known by this older colonial name.

clue.text: Outside broadcast — do watch

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for outside broadcast, a programme made on location
do means serve, as in that will do or that will serve

explanation.surface: A location broadcast: tune in and watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch is to look at attentively, to notice and keep an eye on.
